passage:
Nikita ran the photocopy shop beside the tehsil office in Sangamner, and she read the notice twice between customers: an online shoe store she had used had leaked customer data, 'including partial or full card numbers'.
'Search the bank's helpline,' said Sabina, who was waiting for her photocopies. 'It'll come up.'
Nikita shook her head. She had heard of people calling fake numbers from search results. Instead she took her debit card out of her wallet, turned it over, and dialled the helpline printed on the back.
A recorded menu, then a real person. Nikita explained the breach. The officer blocked the card while she waited, confirmed there were no unknown transactions in the last month, and arranged a new card by post. 'Would you like SMS alerts for every transaction?' Nikita said yes.
Sabina had watched the whole call. 'I'd have searched,' she admitted.
'I nearly did too,' Nikita said, putting the old card in a drawer to cut up later.

qa.a: The helpline printed on the back of her debit card.

qa.q: Why did Nikita shake her head at searching for the helpline?
qa.a: She was wary, having heard of people reaching fake numbers from search results.
Using the official number on the card, blocking it at once, checking recent transactions and turning on alerts.

qa.q: How does the call look to Sabina?
qa.a: Sabina realises she would have searched online, and learns from watching Nikita use the safer route.

grounding: Shows a young person whose card number leaked calling the bank on the number printed on the card, blocking it and setting transaction alerts.

subtype: Approach: contact the bank and freeze cards if financial data is affected [Action]
passage:
Noa was on a bus in São Paulo when the email arrived: a concert-ticket site had been breached, and some customers' card numbers 'may have been exposed'. Her card was on that site.
A minute later, a text: 'Your bank has detected fraud. Call this number to secure your account.' The number wasn't one she recognised.
Noa felt her heart speed up. She almost tapped it. Instead she messaged her brother Paulo: 'Is this real?' He replied at once: 'Don't call that. Use the number on the back of your card.'
She got off at the next stop, sat on a bench and dialled the number printed on her card. The bank's agent confirmed they had sent no text. They blocked the card, checked the last week's payments, found nothing strange, and set up app alerts for every transaction. A new card would come in five days.
Noa deleted the fake text and forwarded the notice to Paulo. 'Your card was on that site too, wasn't it?'

qa.q: When would Noa's new card arrive?
How did Noa feel when the unknown number texted her?
qa.a: Her heart sped up; she felt alarmed and nearly tapped it before stopping to check.

qa.q: Why was calling the number on the card the right move?
qa.a: It reached the real bank, avoiding the fake helpline in the text and letting the card be blocked safely.

qa.q: What might Paulo be thinking when Noa forwards the notice?
qa.a: Paulo may realise his own card could be at risk and feel grateful for the reminder.

grounding: Shows a young person whose card data leaked calling the bank on the card's printed number, blocking it and setting alerts while ignoring a fake helpline.
